title: Introduce staged batcher adapters and compact KV index compaction to reduce tail latency and memory churn
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: The continuous batcher currently couples admission, grouping, and dispatch logic into a single monolithic pipeline. That design simplifies initial implementation but increases tail-latency variance, complicates targeted optimizations, and makes it hard to reason about KV cache warmup and metadata lifetime. Separately, KV index metadata is held in a dense in-memory structure that is expensive to mark/scan during GC spikes and contributes to OOM pressure on high-concurrency workloads.

This ticket proposes two coordinated runtime refactors: 1) split the continuous batcher into a staged set of adapters (admission -> pack -> dispatch) with lightweight per-stage metadata and explicit backpressure/shaping hooks; 2) introduce a compact on-heap KV index plus optional segmented cold-store for rarely used keys to reduce memory churn and GC scanning overhead. Both changes target production stability and cost (reduce 95th latency and memory footprint) without changing the external API surface to customers.
acceptance_criteria: Staged batcher implemented behind a runtime feature-flag with three clear stages: admission, pack, dispatch
Benchmarked 95th-percentile request latency reduced by >= 20% on representative chat workload when staged batcher is enabled
Per-stage metrics emitted to Console (admission_queue_ms, pack_time_ms, dispatch_queue_ms, batch_size_histogram)
Compact KV index reduces RSS and GC pause time by >= 15% under sustained embed/stream workloads
Compatibility: existing model routing, KV get/put semantics, and prefix caching behavior are preserved
Canary rollout plan documented and a rollback knob exists (disable staged batcher and compact index independently)
Code reviewed and merged with at least two approvals and passing e2e perf tests
PRs reference design doc and include microbenchmarks and load test harness configs
